summary: Household: New York; 4 people (you, your wife, your son, your 72-year-old dad); one child under 18 (not under 5); no pregnancy; about $20,000/year earned from work; dad has no Social Security or other income; about $5,000 in savings; you own your home; wife has a back condition that stops her working; no full-time college students. Recommended now: SNAP (food), Medicaid (covers the household at this income level, including the child), EITC, Child Tax Credit (refundable part), and free school meals for your son. Not recommended: WIC (no child under 5 and no pregnancy); ACA premium tax credit (Medicaid covers this income level); TANF (the roughly $5,000 in savings is likely above New York's cash-aid asset limit). Hand off to a caseworker to check two items I could not confirm: whether your wife receives or has applied for SSI/Social Security Disability (she may qualify for SSI or a disability-based benefit), and whether your dad qualifies for SSI on his own assets (SSI has a $2,000 limit for an individual).
